maria: Quick sync — we need a final bench protocol to root-cause the perf regression on long sequences (8k+). Can we agree a reproducible matrix and exact observability artifacts to collect?

aj: +1. My proposal: 1) a small controlled replay (prod sample) 2) a synthetic microbench for kernel-level isolation. Both must use identical container image + driver + env.

ken: Agree. Key invariants: GPU model, CUDA driver, container tag, and our runtime build id. Also record kernel flags and LD_PRELOADs.

sam: For clarity, suggest we enumerate the matrix rows: GPUs=[A100-40GB,H100-80GB], drivers=[515.76,535.54], images=[redwood/runtime:2028-03-02-cuda11.8, redwood/runtime:2028-03-02-cuda12.1], batcher=[continuous,dynamic,none]. That gives a manageable sweep.

nora: Don't forget to capture KV cache metrics. We saw different hit rates in the wild; that changes batching behavior. Metric list: kv_cache_hit_rate, avg_batch_size, tokens/sec, p50/p95 latency, kernel_time_breakdown (matmul, softmax, other).

ben: FYI on an earlier run: H100 + driver 535.54 showed ~12% p95 regression compared to 515.76 for the same model and runtime build. Preliminary nvprof/Nsight traces pointed at cuBLAS algorithm selection changes on large matmuls.

elise: Important: make sure to run the exact same workload ordering. Replay harness should use the same timestamped request sequence, and synthetic should be deterministic (fixed seq lengths + prompt shapes).

maria: Concrete execution command (example):
```
./run_loadtest \
  --harness=replay \
  --replay-file=samples/8k_prod_sample.jsonl \
  --duration=30m \
  --image=redwood/runtime:2028-03-02-cuda11.8 \
  --driver=515.76 \
  --env RW_RUNTIME_BUILD=20280302-7 \
  --env RW_BATCHER_MODE=continuous \
  --collect nsys,trace,kv-metrics \
  --outdir=/tmp/bench/1834001122
```

aj: Two small protocol rules: A) pin GPU clock/profile to baseline; B) run warmup 5 min, then steady 25 min for metrics. Also collect a short Nsight Systems (10s) at a p95 event.

ken: Add a deterministic cuBLAS setting step for comparability. Example envs to capture/set: `CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG`, `CUBLAS_ALGO_SEARCH`, `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=0`, `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO`. Record them in the run metadata.

nora: For KV cache stats: instrument per-request cache hit/miss and prefix reuse count. Also track per-sequence latency by token index to see KV cache warming effects.

ben: On the H100 case I mentioned I forced `CUBLAS_ALGO_SEARCH=FAST` and saw p95 improve back to baseline, so algorithm choice matters. We should include a knob sweep of `CUBLAS_ALGO_SEARCH=[HEURISTIC,FAST,EXHAUSTIVE]` as an optional dimension.

elise: We should also run a short cross-check with synthetic traffic that isolates kernel runtime: single-threaded loader, fixed batch sizes, no KV cache. That helps differentiate runtime batching heuristics from kernel-level regressions.

maria: loadtest-bot kicked off the first matrix job: config /matrix/1834001122. I'll post summaries here. Reminder: label each run with `env:driver:image:gpu:batcher:buildid`.

loadtest-bot: Run complete: /matrix/1834001122/row-3 (H100,535.54,redwood/runtime:2028-03-02-cuda11.8,continuous)
Summary:
- tokens_per_sec: 42.1k
- avg_batch_size: 6.8
- kv_cache_hit_rate: 0.72
- p50_latency: 18ms
- p95_latency: 120ms
- kernel_breakdown: matmul=78ms, softmax=22ms, other=20ms

maria: loadtest-bot summary looks like the same config as Ben's failing run. Ben, can you attach your Nsight snippet?

ben: Attached short Nsight export (s3://redwood-bench/traces/1834001122-h100-535.nsight) — it shows a higher matmul time and different cuBLAS algorithm selected at large N,K.

aj: Next steps agreed: 1) full sweep across drivers for H100 and A100 2) run synthetic kernel-isolation microbench to confirm algorithm timings 3) capture Nsight on one baseline and one failing point 4) store all envs and image digests in the run metadata.

ken: I will add a small post-processing script to compute apples-to-apples comparisons: normalize by TF32 enablement, and compare p95 delta and matmul_time delta. Aim to produce a one-pager for sig-runtime.

nora: I'll add KV-focused replay that emphasizes prefix reuse heavy traffic to surface caching regressions.

maria: timeline: run sweep in next 24h, collect traces, sync tomorrow 10:30 for triage. If we confirm driver-induced regression, we escalate to infra and GPU vendor.

ben: also file a regression ticket with trace links + minimal reproduction (synthetic config + forced cublas knobs).

elise: I'll coordinate trace uploads and make sure images are immutable (digest pinned) in the metadata.

maria: Thanks all — please comment if you want different knobs in the matrix. :eyes:
